# Environment variables that make the extension refuse to connect: the driver's bundled libraries
# apply them to settings the extension does not set, and some can weaken TLS verification. The
# driver loader compiles this list into driver_info.h; the ODBC client checks every name before each
# connect, and the loader checks the load-phase names before it calls the platform loader.
#
# Each name carries the earliest phase in which the driver or a bundled library reads it: load (the
# platform loader call, with the static initialisers it runs), handle (handle allocation; the
# driver's own initialisation runs at the first environment handle, so it counts as handle) or
# connect. A review of the driver's source on every driver update records the phases, and a new
# name is load until a review records a later one. On Windows the loader checks every name here
# before its first LoadLibraryExW, and a DLL's DllMain reads at load, so every row is load there
# whatever its phase.
# In 2.3.0.0 the Kerberos names and GSS_MECH_CONFIG are load: the bundled Kerberos library reads
# them only when GSS runs, but on macOS the system frameworks the driver links, which that review
# leaves out, may read them earlier.
#
# The names change TLS trust or key logging, Kerberos configuration, plugins or tracing, an AWS
# endpoint, the ODBC configuration file, the TLS library, or settings the ODBC client's results
# depend on, or could not be shown harmless. The proxy variables are not refused, as TLS is verified
# end to end, and SSL_CERT_FILE, the ODBC client's trust source, is in known-environment.txt. Every
# driver update reviews this classification.
#
# The environment-name rule fails on a listed name the driver no longer holds, unless the row's
# comment says why it need not be there: "libpq variable, refused even where absent" (the twelve
# libpq variables PGGSSLIB to PGSYSCONFDIR below, which this list always holds), "built at run time
# from <string>" (the per-service endpoint variables, one for each AWS service client or credential
# provider the driver bundles, which the AWS SDK names at run time from the service's identifier),
# or "only in <platform>,...", optionally followed by "; <why it is still refused elsewhere>". That
# list only exempts the row from the rule on the platforms it leaves out: every name here is refused
# on every platform, since driver_info.h compiles the whole list in for each one, which fails
# closed. The platforms are the lock's; each macOS slice is checked as its own (osx_amd64 for
# x86_64, osx_arm64 for arm64).
#
# name           phase
PGGSSLIB         connect  # libpq variable, refused even where absent
PGHOSTADDR       connect
PGKRBSRVNAME     connect
PGOPTIONS        connect
PGREQUIRESSL     connect
PGSERVICE        connect
PGSERVICEFILE    connect
PGSSLCERT        connect
PGSSLCRL         connect
PGSSLKEY         connect
PGSSLROOTCERT    connect
PGSYSCONFDIR     connect
SSLKEYLOGFILE    connect  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,osx_amd64,osx_arm64
SSL_CERT_DIR     connect
KRB5_CONFIG      load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5_TRACE       load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5CCNAME       load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5_KTNAME      load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL connect
ODBCINI          handle  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,osx_amd64,osx_arm64
PGCLIENTENCODING connect
PGDATESTYLE      connect
PGTZ             connect
PGGEQO           connect
PGTTY            connect
PGAUTHTYPE       connect
PGSSLSNI         connect
KRB5_CLIENT_KTNAME  load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5_KDC_PROFILE load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5RCACHEDIR    load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5RCACHENAME   load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
KRB5RCACHETYPE   load  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,windows_amd64; on macOS the system Kerberos.framework, which the driver links, may read it
CURL_SSL_BACKEND connect  # only in linux_amd64,linux_arm64,osx_amd64,osx_arm64
AWS_PROXY_NO_VERIFY_PEER  connect
AWS_CSM_ENABLED  connect
AWS_CSM_HOST     connect
AWS_CSM_PORT     connect
AWS_COMMON_AVX2  connect  # only in linux_amd64,windows_amd64
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_REDSHIFT  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_REDSHIFT_SERVERLESS  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_SSO  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_SSO_OAUTH  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_SIGNIN  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_STS  connect  # built at run time from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_
GSS_MECH_CONFIG  load
S2N_INTEG_TEST   connect
S2N_DONT_MLOCK   connect
